channel.title: Cortrix Blog
channel.description: Practical readings of foundational papers on semantic systems and agent memory.

item.title: DBpedia explained: why linked data still matters
item.description: Why stable identities and linked data still matter when your agents retrieve knowledge from different systems.
item.dc:creator: Scott

item.title: TransE explained: relationships beyond vector similarity
item.description: What the simple h + r ≈ t formula tells us about relationships in a knowledge graph, and what a similarity score leaves out.
item.dc:creator: Scott

item.title: RAG explained: external memory brings data governance back
item.description: RAG lets a model use external knowledge. The original paper also helps explain why sources, updates, and data governance still matter.
item.dc:creator: Scott

item.title: Reflexion explained: agent memory without weight updates
item.description: Reflexion turns feedback into memory without changing model weights. Its most useful lesson may be about the evaluator.
item.dc:creator: Scott

item.title: HippoRAG explained: why RAG comes back to knowledge graphs
item.description: HippoRAG connects clues across documents with a knowledge graph. Here is how it works, and where the graph can go wrong.
item.dc:creator: Scott
